Combine the estimates of two samples

Source: R/hc3_stats.R
combine_two_samples.Rd

Fixed-effect (inverse-variance) combination of per-sample estimates, one pair per combination of the by columns, with a normal p-value, Cochran's Q heterogeneity test (1 df) and I2. replication_p is the larger of the two per-sample p-values when both estimates have the same non-zero sign and 1 otherwise: evidence that both samples support the effect.

Usage

combine_two_samples(tab, by, sample_col = "sample", failed = c("keep", "drop"))

Arguments

tab

data.frame of per-sample fits with columns beta, se, p, the by columns, the sample column and optionally status, e.g. the stacked output of fit_ols_hc3(). Exactly two samples, each once per combination of by.

by

Columns identifying one test.

sample_col

Column holding the sample name.

failed

"keep": failed pairs stay in the result with beta/se NA, p = 1, replication_p = 1 and status = "fit_failed", so they count in later multiple-testing corrections; "drop" removes them.

Value

A data.frame with one row per test (in order of first appearance): the by columns, beta, se, p, replication_p, same_direction, Q, heterogeneity_p, I2, status, and beta_<sample>, se_<sample>, p_<sample> for both samples (sorted by name).

Details

A pair is failed when a standard error is missing or not positive or, if tab has a status column, when a status is not "ok". Combining two samples does not add biological replicates.

Examples

fits <- data.frame(gene = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 2),
                   sample = rep(c("s1", "s2"), 2),
                   beta = c(0.5, 0.4, 0.3, -0.2), se = c(0.1, 0.12, 0.1, 0.1),
                   p = c(1e-6, 1e-3, 3e-3, 0.05))
combine_two_samples(fits, by = "gene")
#>   gene      beta         se            p replication_p same_direction
#> 1    a 0.4590164 0.07682213 2.300134e-09         0.001           TRUE
#> 2    b 0.0500000 0.07071068 4.795001e-01         1.000          FALSE
#>            Q heterogeneity_p   I2 status beta_s1 se_s1  p_s1 beta_s2 se_s2
#> 1  0.4098361     0.522052724 0.00     ok     0.5   0.1 1e-06     0.4  0.12
#> 2 12.5000000     0.000406952 0.92     ok     0.3   0.1 3e-03    -0.2  0.10
#>    p_s2
#> 1 0.001
#> 2 0.050
